title: Add Admin backend: permissions, lifecycle writes, read-model, bespoke router, demo wiring
description: No schema migration needed -- app_user/role/role_permission/audit_log already exist from TASK-024. src/auth/permissions.ts gains usersRead/usersManage/rolesRead/rolesWrite keys. src/auth/lifecycle.ts gains setUserActiveWithin (rejects self-disable), createRoleWithin (unique name per master, isSuperadmin always false), setRolePermissionWithin (rejects editing the superadmin role, validates permissionKey against Object.values(PERMISSIONS)) -- all audited via appendAudit, mirroring lifecycle.ts's existing createInvitation/acceptInvitation style exactly. src/api/admin.ts (new) provides listCompanyUsers (real appUser+userCompany+role joined for the company, UNIONed with pending userInvitation rows), listRoles, listRolePermissions, listAuditLog (paginated, actor name resolved) -- mirrors src/api/dashboard.ts's plain-function shape, no ResourceDefinition. src/api/routes/admin.ts (new) exposes GET /api/admin/users, POST /api/admin/users/:userId/actions/toggle-active, POST /api/admin/invitations (reuses existing createInvitation), GET/POST /api/admin/roles, GET /api/admin/role-permissions, POST /api/admin/roles/:roleId/actions/set-permission, GET /api/admin/audit-log -- mirrors routes/auth.ts's manual hasPermission+scope style, not the generic resource dispatcher (deliberately: these tables are excluded from RLS company-scope by design per deploy/sql/production-rls.sql, and structurally don't fit ResourceDefinition's single-id-column cursor pagination -- appUser's PK is userId, role's is roleId, role_permission has a composite PK with no id column at all). Mounted in src/api/app.ts alongside /api/auth and /api/setup. Demo side: erp-demo-runtime-impl.ts gains matching commands (createInvitation needs a demo-only fixed LifecycleOptions token key + publicUrl, mirroring how the production integration test already supplies a fixed key). erp-system-data-adapter.js exposes the real signed-in appUser.userId as state.activeUserId (already available as activeUser.user_id in readPayload()'s d.users query, just not currently surfaced), special-cases list()/create()/action() for admin/users, admin/roles, admin/role-permissions, admin/audit-log, admin/invitations (NOT added to RESOURCE_TABLES, matching the bespoke-not-generic decision), and -- the key structural fix found during research -- adds appendAudit-equivalent calls at the single generic create()/action() dispatch chokepoint using state.activeUserId, since appendAudit today is only ever called from the production HTTP layer (actionDispatcher.ts/routes/resources.ts/routes/auth.ts/lifecycle.ts/completeSetup.ts) and never by any src/modules/** business module directly, meaning audit_log has been permanently empty in browser demo mode for every module, not just this one -- this one mechanical addition retroactively gives every existing Canonical write (asset creation, PO receipt, etc.) a real demo-mode audit trail too. DONE 2026-07-19: implemented mostly as planned, with two real corrections found during implementation (both documented here since the plan didn't anticipate them). (1) node:crypto boundary: lifecycle.ts hard-imports ./password and ./tokenCrypto (node:crypto), so importing anything from it into web/src/erp-demo-runtime-impl.ts made npm run build:demo fail outright ('randomBytes is not exported by __vite-browser-external') -- not just a warning. Fixed by extracting AuthLifecycleError into a dependency-free src/auth/authErrors.ts, and moving setUserActiveWithin/createRoleWithin/setRolePermissionWithin plus a new demo-only createInvitationRecordWithin (Web Crypto token instead of encryptToken/newOpaqueToken, no outbox event -- nothing in-browser would ever consume it) into a new src/auth/adminLifecycle.ts with a verified-clean (no node:crypto) import graph. (2) transaction nesting: the demo adapter always pre-wraps *Within calls in its own requireDemoDb().transaction(function(tx){...}), but my first draft of the 3 admin-lifecycle functions self-transacted via withTenantTransaction internally -- calling .transaction() on an already-in-progress PGlite transaction throws 'this.client.transaction is not a function'. Fixed by splitting each into a raw-exec ...Within(exec,...) core (no transaction-opening, matches every other module's convention exactly) plus a thin self-transacting wrapper (setUserActive/createRole/setRolePermission) for routes/admin.ts, which calls with a top-level db exactly like routes/auth.ts already calls createInvitation. Also found and fixed a double-audit bug live in-browser: the generic recordDemoAudit chokepoint in erp-system-data-adapter.js's create()/action() wrappers was firing for admin/* resources even though their business logic already self-audits (matching production, where routes/admin.ts never audits a second time either) -- fixed by skipping entity.indexOf('admin/')===0 in recordDemoAudit. Full suite green: typecheck x2, npm test 163 passed/1 skipped (6 new tests in src/auth/adminLifecycle.test.ts, split from lifecycle.test.ts to match the file split), npm run demo, npm run build:demo (clean, no node:crypto errors), check:demo-schema/check:drift (no migration needed, 0 drift), npm run audit:screens (114 routes, 50 canonical unchanged -- screens are TASK-042), npm run smoke. Manually verified in a real PGlite browser session (window.ErpSystemData.reset()): admin/users, admin/roles, admin/role-permissions, admin/audit-log all return real seeded data (2 users, 2 roles, Viewer's 9 real permission grants); created a role, granted it a permission, toggled a user off and back on, created an invitation -- all real writes, all succeeded; confirmed the demo-mode audit-log fix works end-to-end by creating an unrelated asset and seeing a real audit_log row appear (entity 'assets/assets', actor 'Admin'); confirmed exactly one audit row per write after the double-audit fix (6 writes -> 6 rows, not 12).

Add a tenant-scoped master_module table (master_fn + module_key + enabled) via Drizzle migration, business logic to list/set a master's enabled modules (mirroring adminLifecycle.ts's raw-exec-Within + self-transacting-wrapper split), a new admin.modules.manage permission, and bespoke /api/admin/modules routes mirroring routes/admin.ts.
acceptance: Drizzle migration adds master_module (master_fn, module_key, enabled) with an appropriate composite key/index
Business logic provides listMasterModules/setMasterModuleWithin, audited, gated on a new admin.modules.manage permission
GET/POST /api/admin/modules routes exist, mounted in src/api/app.ts, mirroring routes/admin.ts's style
Demo adapter gains matching admin/modules bespoke dispatch (not a generic resource)
New unit tests cover tenant isolation and the permission gate
npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run demo, npm run build:demo all pass

title: Wire module-activation-control screen + enforce gating
description: Wire module-activation-control to the real backend from TASK-047 instead of localStorage. Enforce the toggle in two places, not just the UI: hide a disabled module from the sidebar/module shell for non-superadmin users of a restricted master_fn, and reject API-mode requests to that module's resources/actions server-side (a client-only toggle would not meet the stated requirement that a client can be genuinely restricted to e.g. Sales-only).
acceptance: module-activation-control reads/writes the real /api/admin/modules (or demo equivalent) backend
Disabling a module server-side hides its sidebar entry and blocks its routes/resources for a non-superadmin test user of that master_fn, verified live
Superadmin's own access is never restricted by this mechanism
npm run audit:screens passes; route moves to CANONICAL_SCREEN_ROUTES/API_SCREEN_ROUTES
Live browser check desktop+375px, zero console errors: toggle a module off, confirm it disappears from a restricted user's sidebar; toggle back on, confirm it reappears
